Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. - **PR #**: 752
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/752
- **Title**: gh-750 Machine PR + validation_failed = permanent park: no self-clear path (live: fa #1227)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-750` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +268
- **Deletions**: -2
- **Created**: 2026-10-05T18:48:53Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-05T18:48:53Z

## PR Description

Closes #750
### What changed
A MACHINE-authored PR parked on `validation_failed` now has a self-clear path: `update_branch`'s sticky-park RESET probe clears the label when the current head's check rollup is **green**, or the head **moved past the park** carrying no red dispatched verdict of its own — validate-armed re-validates normally on the next pass.

### Key decisions
- Implemented in the shared `update_branch` RESET probe, so both routes reach it: `silent-update-behind` (BEHIND heads) and `park-reset` (any merge state — the route fa#1227 actually rides)
- Machine-only: guests keep the 2026-09-27 sticky behavior (green-now and machine pushes clear nothing for them); a moved head with its **own** red verdict keeps the park (red never transfers across shas)
- Fail closed: probe failures (park time, actor, verdict) keep the park; the new branch is gated on the same non-null probes the human-push reset demands
- Verified ticket item (a): both `validation_failed` SET paths (`update_branch` sticky-park, `fail_validation` guest park) are guest-gated — the label on fa#1227 is legacy residue, no current rule labels machine PRs

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
```
7 new tests in the sticky-park suite: machine + green head self-clears (fa#1227 regression), head-moved-past-park self-clears, head predates park holds, own-red-verdict holds, probe failure holds (fail closed), guest sticky park untouched, park-reset rule route works.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    PR[Machine PR parked: validation_failed] --> PRST{park-reset rule}
    PRST --> R[update_branch RESET probe]
    R --> G{Head rollup GREEN?}
    G -->|yes| CLR[Remove label + clear comment]
    G -->|no| M{Head moved past park, no own red verdict?}
    M -->|yes| CLR
    M -->|no| HOLD[Park holds — fail closed]
    CLR --> VA[validate-armed re-validates next pass]
```

</details>

- **State**: open

- **Updated**: 2026-10-05T18:48:53Z

## PR Description

Closes #750
### What changed
A MACHINE-authored PR parked on `validation_failed` now has a self-clear path: `update_branch`'s sticky-park RESET probe clears the label when the current head's check rollup is **green**, or the head **moved past the park** carrying no red dispatched verdict of its own — validate-armed re-validates normally on the next pass.

### Key decisions
- Implemented in the shared `update_branch` RESET probe, so both routes reach it: `silent-update-behind` (BEHIND heads) and `park-reset` (any merge state — the route fa#1227 actually rides)
- Machine-only: guests keep the 2026-09-27 sticky behavior (green-now and machine pushes clear nothing for them); a moved head with its **own** red verdict keeps the park (red never transfers across shas)
- Fail closed: probe failures (park time, actor, verdict) keep the park; the new branch is gated on the same non-null probes the human-push reset demands
- Verified ticket item (a): both `validation_failed` SET paths (`update_branch` sticky-park, `fail_validation` guest park) are guest-gated — the label on fa#1227 is legacy residue, no current rule labels machine PRs

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
```
7 new tests in the sticky-park suite: machine + green head self-clears (fa#1227 regression), head-moved-past-park self-clears, head predates park holds, own-red-verdict holds, probe failure holds (fail closed), guest sticky park untouched, park-reset rule route works.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    PR[Machine PR parked: validation_failed] --> PRST{park-reset rule}
    PRST --> R[update_branch RESET probe]
    R --> G{Head rollup GREEN?}
    G -->|yes| CLR[Remove label + clear comment]
    G -->|no| M{Head moved past park, no own red verdict?}
    M -->|yes| CLR
    M -->|no| HOLD[Park holds — fail closed]
    CLR --> VA[validate-armed re-validates next pass]
```

</details>

A MACHINE-authored PR parked on `validation_failed` now has a self-clear path: `update_branch`'s sticky-park RESET probe clears the label when the current head's check rollup is **green**, or the head **moved past the park** carrying no red dispatched verdict of its own — validate-armed re-validates normally on the next pass.

### Key decisions
- Implemented in the shared `update_branch` RESET probe, so both routes reach it: `silent-update-behind` (BEHIND heads) and `park-reset` (any merge state — the route fa#1227 actually rides)

- Verified ticket item (a): both `validation_failed` SET paths (`update_branch` sticky-park, `fail_validation` guest park) are guest-gated — the label on fa#1227 is legacy residue, no current rule labels machine PRs

## PR Description

Closes #750
### What changed
A MACHINE-authored PR parked on `validation_failed` now has a self-clear path: `update_branch`'s sticky-park RESET probe clears the label when the current head's check rollup is **green**, or the head **moved past the park** carrying no red dispatched verdict of its own — validate-armed re-validates normally on the next pass.

### Key decisions
- Implemented in the shared `update_branch` RESET probe, so both routes reach it: `silent-update-behind` (BEHIND heads) and `park-reset` (any merge state — the route fa#1227 actually rides)
- Machine-only: guests keep the 2026-09-27 sticky behavior (green-now and machine pushes clear nothing for them); a moved head with its **own** red verdict keeps the park (red never transfers across shas)
- Fail closed: probe failures (park time, actor, verdict) keep the park; the new branch is gated on the same non-null probes the human-push reset demands
- Verified ticket item (a): both `validation_failed` SET paths (`update_branch` sticky-park, `fail_validation` guest park) are guest-gated — the label on fa#1227 is legacy residue, no current rule labels machine PRs

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
```
7 new tests in the sticky-park suite: machine + green head self-clears (fa#1227 regression), head-moved-past-park self-clears, head predates park holds, own-red-verdict holds, probe failure holds (fail closed), guest sticky park untouched, park-reset rule route works.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    PR[Machine PR parked: validation_failed] --> PRST{park-reset rule}

    R --> G{Head rollup GREEN?}
    G -->|yes| CLR[Remove label + clear comment]
    G -->|no| M{Head moved past park, no own red verdict?}
    M -->|yes| CLR
    M -->|no| HOLD[Park holds — fail closed]
    CLR --> VA[validate-armed re-validates next pass]
```

## PR Description

Closes #750
### What changed
A MACHINE-authored PR parked on `validation_failed` now has a self-clear path: `update_branch`'s sticky-park RESET probe clears the label when the current head's check rollup is **green**, or the head **moved past the park** carrying no red dispatched verdict of its own — validate-armed re-validates normally on the next pass.

### Key decisions
- Implemented in the shared `update_branch` RESET probe, so both routes reach it: `silent-update-behind` (BEHIND heads) and `park-reset` (any merge state — the route fa#1227 actually rides)
- Machine-only: guests keep the 2026-09-27 sticky behavior (green-now and machine pushes clear nothing for them); a moved head with its **own** red verdict keeps the park (red never transfers across shas)
- Fail closed: probe failures (park time, actor, verdict) keep the park; the new branch is gated on the same non-null probes the human-push reset demands
- Verified ticket item (a): both `validation_failed` SET paths (`update_branch` sticky-park, `fail_validation` guest park) are guest-gated — the label on fa#1227 is legacy residue, no current rule labels machine PRs

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
```
7 new tests in the sticky-park suite: machine + green head self-clears (fa#1227 regression), head-moved-past-park self-clears, head predates park holds, own-red-verdict holds, probe failure holds (fail closed), guest sticky park untouched, park-reset rule route works.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    PR[Machine PR parked: validation_failed] --> PRST{park-reset rule}
    PRST --> R[update_branch RESET probe]
    R --> G{Head rollup GREEN?}
    G -->|yes| CLR[Remove label + clear comment]
    G -->|no| M{Head moved past park, no own red verdict?}
    M -->|yes| CLR
    M -->|no| HOLD[Park holds — fail closed]
    CLR --> VA[validate-armed re-validates next pass]
```

</details>

## PR Description

Closes #750
### What changed
A MACHINE-authored PR parked on `validation_failed` now has a self-clear path: `update_branch`'s sticky-park RESET probe clears the label when the current head's check rollup is **green**, or the head **moved past the park** carrying no red dispatched verdict of its own — validate-armed re-validates normally on the next pass.

### Key decisions
- Implemented in the shared `update_branch` RESET probe, so both routes reach it: `silent-update-behind` (BEHIND heads) and `park-reset` (any merge state — the route fa#1227 actually rides)
- Machine-only: guests keep the 2026-09-27 sticky behavior (green-now and machine pushes clear nothing for them); a moved head with its **own** red verdict keeps the park (red never transfers across shas)
- Fail closed: probe failures (park time, actor, verdict) keep the park; the new branch is gated on the same non-null probes the human-push reset demands
- Verified ticket item (a): both `validation_failed` SET paths (`update_branch` sticky-park, `fail_validation` guest park) are guest-gated — the label on fa#1227 is legacy residue, no current rule labels machine PRs

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
```
7 new tests in the sticky-park suite: machine + green head self-clears (fa#1227 regression), head-moved-past-park self-clears, head predates park holds, own-red-verdict holds, probe failure holds (fail closed), guest sticky park untouched, park-reset rule route works.

```mermaid
flowchart TD

    R --> G{Head rollup GREEN?}
    G -->|yes| CLR[Remove label + clear comment]
    G -->|no| M{Head moved past park, no own red verdict?}
    M -->|yes| CLR
    M -->|no| HOLD[Park holds — fail closed]
    CLR --> VA[validate-armed re-validates next pass]
```

## PR Description

Closes #750
### What changed
A MACHINE-authored PR parked on `validation_failed` now has a self-clear path: `update_branch`'s sticky-park RESET probe clears the label when the current head's check rollup is **green**, or the head **moved past the park** carrying no red dispatched verdict of its own — validate-armed re-validates normally on the next pass.

### Key decisions
- Implemented in the shared `update_branch` RESET probe, so both routes reach it: `silent-update-behind` (BEHIND heads) and `park-reset` (any merge state — the route fa#1227 actually rides)
- Machine-only: guests keep the 2026-09-27 sticky behavior (green-now and machine pushes clear nothing for them); a moved head with its **own** red verdict keeps the park (red never transfers across shas)
- Fail closed: probe failures (park time, actor, verdict) keep the park; the new branch is gated on the same non-null probes the human-push reset demands
- Verified ticket item (a): both `validation_failed` SET paths (`update_branch` sticky-park, `fail_validation` guest park) are guest-gated — the label on fa#1227 is legacy residue, no current rule labels machine PRs

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
```
7 new tests in the sticky-park suite: machine + green head self-clears (fa#1227 regression), head-moved-past-park self-clears, head predates park holds, own-red-verdict holds, probe failure holds (fail closed), guest sticky park untouched, park-reset rule route works.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    PR[Machine PR parked: validation_failed] --> PRST{park-reset rule}
    PRST --> R[update_branch RESET probe]
    R --> G{Head rollup GREEN?}
    G -->|yes| CLR[Remove label + clear comment]
    G -->|no| M{Head moved past park, no own red verdict?}
    M -->|yes| CLR
    M -->|no| HOLD[Park holds — fail closed]
    CLR --> VA[validate-armed re-validates next pass]
```

</details>

- **State**: open

- **Updated**: 2026-10-05T18:48:53Z

## PR Description

Closes #750
### What changed
A MACHINE-authored PR parked on `validation_failed` now has a self-clear path: `update_branch`'s sticky-park RESET probe clears the label when the current head's check rollup is **green**, or the head **moved past the park** carrying no red dispatched verdict of its own — validate-armed re-validates normally on the next pass.

### Key decisions
- Implemented in the shared `update_branch` RESET probe, so both routes reach it: `silent-update-behind` (BEHIND heads) and `park-reset` (any merge state — the route fa#1227 actually rides)
- Machine-only: guests keep the 2026-09-27 sticky behavior (green-now and machine pushes clear nothing for them); a moved head with its **own** red verdict keeps the park (red never transfers across shas)
- Fail closed: probe failures (park time, actor, verdict) keep the park; the new branch is gated on the same non-null probes the human-push reset demands
- Verified ticket item (a): both `validation_failed` SET paths (`update_branch` sticky-park, `fail_validation` guest park) are guest-gated — the label on fa#1227 is legacy residue, no current rule labels machine PRs

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
```
7 new tests in the sticky-park suite: machine + green head self-clears (fa#1227 regression), head-moved-past-park self-clears, head predates park holds, own-red-verdict holds, probe failure holds (fail closed), guest sticky park untouched, park-reset rule route works.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    PR[Machine PR parked: validation_failed] --> PRST{park-reset rule}
    PRST --> R[update_branch RESET probe]
    R --> G{Head rollup GREEN?}
    G -->|yes| CLR[Remove label + clear comment]
    G -->|no| M{Head moved past park, no own red verdict?}
    M -->|yes| CLR
    M -->|no| HOLD[Park holds — fail closed]
    CLR --> VA[validate-armed re-validates next pass]
```

</details>

## PR Description

Closes #750
### What changed
A MACHINE-authored PR parked on `validation_failed` now has a self-clear path: `update_branch`'s sticky-park RESET probe clears the label when the current head's check rollup is **green**, or the head **moved past the park** carrying no red dispatched verdict of its own — validate-armed re-validates normally on the next pass.

### Key decisions
- Implemented in the shared `update_branch` RESET probe, so both routes reach it: `silent-update-behind` (BEHIND heads) and `park-reset` (any merge state — the route fa#1227 actually rides)
- Machine-only: guests keep the 2026-09-27 sticky behavior (green-now and machine pushes clear nothing for them); a moved head with its **own** red verdict keeps the park (red never transfers across shas)
- Fail closed: probe failures (park time, actor, verdict) keep the park; the new branch is gated on the same non-null probes the human-push reset demands
- Verified ticket item (a): both `validation_failed` SET paths (`update_branch` sticky-park, `fail_validation` guest park) are guest-gated — the label on fa#1227 is legacy residue, no current rule labels machine PRs

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
```
7 new tests in the sticky-park suite: machine + green head self-clears (fa#1227 regression), head-moved-past-park self-clears, head predates park holds, own-red-verdict holds, probe failure holds (fail closed), guest sticky park untouched, park-reset rule route works.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    PR[Machine PR parked: validation_failed] --> PRST{park-reset rule}
    PRST --> R[update_branch RESET probe]
    R --> G{Head rollup GREEN?}
    G -->|yes| CLR[Remove label + clear comment]
    G -->|no| M{Head moved past park, no own red verdict?}
    M -->|yes| CLR
    M -->|no| HOLD[Park holds — fail closed]
    CLR --> VA[validate-armed re-validates next pass]
```

</details>

Note the new code uses `headActorVf.date` — that's the committer date of the head commit. For a silent-update merge commit, committer date = when the SM ran silent update. So the headMovedCleanVf for a parked machine PR behind main: the SM silent-updates the branch (merge commit by sm-silent-update), which moves the head. Then headCommitActor on the new head returns the MERGE commit (committer sm-silent-update, date = merge time > park time). So `headTsVf > parkedTsVf` is TRUE. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. ## PR Description

Closes #750
### What changed
A MACHINE-authored PR parked on `validation_failed` now has a self-clear path: `update_branch`'s sticky-park RESET probe clears the label when the current head's check rollup is **green**, or the head **moved past the park** carrying no red dispatched verdict of its own — validate-armed re-validates normally on the next pass.

### Key decisions
- Implemented in the shared `update_branch` RESET probe, so both routes reach it: `silent-update-behind` (BEHIND heads) and `park-reset` (any merge state — the route fa#1227 actually rides)
- Machine-only: guests keep the 2026-09-27 sticky behavior (green-now and machine pushes clear nothing for them); a moved head with its **own** red verdict keeps the park (red never transfers across shas)
- Fail closed: probe failures (park time, actor, verdict) keep the park; the new branch is gated on the same non-null probes the human-push reset demands
- Verified ticket item (a): both `validation_failed` SET paths (`update_branch` sticky-park, `fail_validation` guest park) are guest-gated — the label on fa#1227 is legacy residue, no current rule labels machine PRs

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
```
7 new tests in the sticky-park suite: machine + green head self-clears (fa#1227 regression), head-moved-past-park self-clears, head predates park holds, own-red-verdict holds, probe failure holds (fail closed), guest sticky park untouched, park-reset rule route works.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    PR[Machine PR parked: validation_failed] --> PRST{park-reset rule}
    PRST --> R[update_branch RESET probe]
    R --> G{Head rollup GREEN?}
    G -->|yes| CLR[Remove label + clear comment]
    G -->|no| M{Head moved past park, no own red verdict?}
    M -->|yes| CLR
    M -->|no| HOLD[Park holds — fail closed]
    CLR --> VA[validate-armed re-validates next pass]
```

</details>

Note the new code uses `headActorVf.date` — that's the committer date of the head commit. For a silent-update merge commit, committer date = when the SM ran silent update. So the headMovedCleanVf for a parked machine PR behind main: the SM silent-updates the branch (merge commit by sm-silent-update), which moves the head. Then headCommitActor on the new head returns the MERGE commit (committer sm-silent-update, date = merge time > park time). So `headTsVf > parkedTsVf` is TRUE. And latestDispatchedVerdict on the new sha — parked PRs get no CI dispatch, so null ≠ 'failure' → true. So headMovedCleanVf fires.

That's per the ticket spec: "the park predates the last head move". OK, intended.

6. **Now — a deeper design question: `validationRollupGreen` returns true only when `checkConclusion === 'green'`. For a PR with NO checks at all (checkConclusion 'none'), green is false — falls to headMovedCleanVf. Fine.**

re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. ## PR Description

Closes #750
### What changed
A MACHINE-authored PR parked on `validation_failed` now has a self-clear path: `update_branch`'s sticky-park RESET probe clears the label when the current head's check rollup is **green**, or the head **moved past the park** carrying no red dispatched verdict of its own — validate-armed re-validates normally on the next pass.

### Key decisions
- Implemented in the shared `update_branch` RESET probe, so both routes reach it: `silent-update-behind` (BEHIND heads) and `park-reset` (any merge state — the route fa#1227 actually rides)
- Machine-only: guests keep the 2026-09-27 sticky behavior (green-now and machine pushes clear nothing for them); a moved head with its **own** red verdict keeps the park (red never transfers across shas)
- Fail closed: probe failures (park time, actor, verdict) keep the park; the new branch is gated on the same non-null probes the human-push reset demands
- Verified ticket item (a): both `validation_failed` SET paths (`update_branch` sticky-park, `fail_validation` guest park) are guest-gated — the label on fa#1227 is legacy residue, no current rule labels machine PRs

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
```
7 new tests in the sticky-park suite: machine + green head self-clears (fa#1227 regression), head-moved-past-park self-clears, head predates park holds, own-red-verdict holds, probe failure holds (fail closed), guest sticky park untouched, park-reset rule route works.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    PR[Machine PR parked: validation_failed] --> PRST{park-reset rule}
    PRST --> R[update_branch RESET probe]
    R --> G{Head rollup GREEN?}
    G -->|yes| CLR[Remove label + clear comment]
    G -->|no| M{Head moved past park, no own red verdict?}
    M -->|yes| CLR
    M -->|no| HOLD[Park holds — fail closed]
    CLR --> VA[validate-armed re-validates next pass]
```

</details>

Note the new code uses `headActorVf.date` — that's the committer date of the head commit. For a silent-update merge commit, committer date = when the SM ran silent update. So the headMovedCleanVf for a parked machine PR behind main: the SM silent-updates the branch (merge commit by sm-silent-update), which moves the head. Then headCommitActor on the new head returns the MERGE commit (committer sm-silent-update, date = merge time > park time). So `headTsVf > parkedTsVf` is TRUE. And latestDispatchedVerdict on the new sha — parked PRs get no CI dispatch, so null ≠ 'failure' → true. So headMovedCleanVf fires.

   So on the very first tick after the park was set (for a machine PR behind main), the sequence would be: park set (in the era when machine PRs could get labeled — legacy), then the next tick: update_branch runs (BEHIND), silent update moves the head, and the machine self-clear clears the label. That's per the ticket spec: "the park predates the last head move". OK, intended.

   BUT — there's a subtle wrinkle: the ladder order. The `machineUnparkVf` computation happens BEFORE `silentUpdateBranch(ticket.branch)` is called (the silent update happens after the whole park ladder at the end of update_branch). So on each tick, the probe reads the head as of this tick. Fine.

5. **Now the most important check: does the GREEN rollup path use `prStatus` which may be STALE (keyed to an older head)?** `provider.prStatus(prNumber)` — a fresh GitHub call returns the current head's check conclusion. OK.

6. **Now — a deeper design question: `validationRollupGreen` returns true only when `checkConclusion === 'green'`. For a PR with NO checks at all (checkConclusion 'none'), green is false — falls to headMovedCleanVf. Fine.**

7. **Test coverage check**: 7 tests, all reasonable. But is there a test where the machine PR is NOT behind — i.e. the park-reset rule route (test 7). Yes.

8. **Edge: `machineUnparkVf` when `headChangedNoVerdictVf` is false because parkedHeadVf is null (legacy park)** — the new path covers. Good.

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,

callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. ## PR Description

Closes #750
### What changed
A MACHINE-authored PR parked on `validation_failed` now has a self-clear path: `update_branch`'s sticky-park RESET probe clears the label when the current head's check rollup is **green**, or the head **moved past the park** carrying no red dispatched verdict of its own — validate-armed re-validates normally on the next pass.

### Key decisions
- Implemented in the shared `update_branch` RESET probe, so both routes reach it: `silent-update-behind` (BEHIND heads) and `park-reset` (any merge state — the route fa#1227 actually rides)
- Machine-only: guests keep the 2026-09-27 sticky behavior (green-now and machine pushes clear nothing for them); a moved head with its **own** red verdict keeps the park (red never transfers across shas)
- Fail closed: probe failures (park time, actor, verdict) keep the park; the new branch is gated on the same non-null probes the human-push reset demands
- Verified ticket item (a): both `validation_failed` SET paths (`update_branch` sticky-park, `fail_validation` guest park) are guest-gated — the label on fa#1227 is legacy residue, no current rule labels machine PRs

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
```
7 new tests in the sticky-park suite: machine + green head self-clears (fa#1227 regression), head-moved-past-park self-clears, head predates park holds, own-red-verdict holds, probe failure holds (fail closed), guest sticky park untouched, park-reset rule route works.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    PR[Machine PR parked: validation_failed] --> PRST{park-reset rule}
    PRST --> R[update_branch RESET probe]
    R --> G{Head rollup GREEN?}
    G -->|yes| CLR[Remove label + clear comment]
    G -->|no| M{Head moved past park, no own red verdict?}
    M -->|yes| CLR
    M -->|no| HOLD[Park holds — fail closed]
    CLR --> VA[validate-armed re-validates next pass]
```

</details>

Note the new code uses `headActorVf.date` — that's the committer date of the head commit. For a silent-update merge commit, committer date = when the SM ran silent update. So the headMovedCleanVf for a parked machine PR behind main: the SM silent-updates the branch (merge commit by sm-silent-update), which moves the head. Then headCommitActor on the new head returns the MERGE commit (committer sm-silent-update, date = merge time > park time). So `headTsVf > parkedTsVf` is TRUE. And latestDispatchedVerdict on the new sha — parked PRs get no CI dispatch, so null ≠ 'failure' → true. So headMovedCleanVf fires.

   So on the very first tick after the park was set (for a machine PR behind main), the sequence would be: park set (in the era when machine PRs could get labeled — legacy), then the next tick: update_branch runs (BEHIND), silent update moves the head, and the machine self-clear clears the label. That's per the ticket spec: "the park predates the last head move". OK, intended.

   BUT — there's a subtle wrinkle: the ladder order. The `machineUnparkVf` computation happens BEFORE `silentUpdateBranch(ticket.branch)` is called (the silent update happens after the whole park ladder at the end of update_branch). So on each tick, the probe reads the head as of this tick. Fine.

5. **Now the most important check: does the GREEN rollup path use `prStatus` which may be STALE (keyed to an older head)?** `provider.prStatus(prNumber)` — a fresh GitHub call returns the current head's check conclusion. OK.

6. **Now — a deeper design question: `validationRollupGreen` returns true only when `checkConclusion === 'green'`. For a PR with NO checks at all (checkConclusion 'none'), green is false — falls to headMovedCleanVf. Fine.**

7. **Test coverage check**: 7 tests, all reasonable. But is there a test where the machine PR is NOT behind — i.e. the park-reset rule route (test 7). Yes.

8. **Edge: `machineUnparkVf` when `headChangedNoVerdictVf` is false because parkedHeadVf is null (legacy park)** — the new path covers. Good.

All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. ## PR Description

Closes #750
### What changed
A MACHINE-authored PR parked on `validation_failed` now has a self-clear path: `update_branch`'s sticky-park RESET probe clears the label when the current head's check rollup is **green**, or the head **moved past the park** carrying no red dispatched verdict of its own — validate-armed re-validates normally on the next pass.

### Key decisions
- Implemented in the shared `update_branch` RESET probe, so both routes reach it: `silent-update-behind` (BEHIND heads) and `park-reset` (any merge state — the route fa#1227 actually rides)
- Machine-only: guests keep the 2026-09-27 sticky behavior (green-now and machine pushes clear nothing for them); a moved head with its **own** red verdict keeps the park (red never transfers across shas)
- Fail closed: probe failures (park time, actor, verdict) keep the park; the new branch is gated on the same non-null probes the human-push reset demands
- Verified ticket item (a): both `validation_failed` SET paths (`update_branch` sticky-park, `fail_validation` guest park) are guest-gated — the label on fa#1227 is legacy residue, no current rule labels machine PRs

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
```
7 new tests in the sticky-park suite: machine + green head self-clears (fa#1227 regression), head-moved-past-park self-clears, head predates park holds, own-red-verdict holds, probe failure holds (fail closed), guest sticky park untouched, park-reset rule route works.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    PR[Machine PR parked: validation_failed] --> PRST{park-reset rule}
    PRST --> R[update_branch RESET probe]
    R --> G{Head rollup GREEN?}
    G -->|yes| CLR[Remove label + clear comment]
    G -->|no| M{Head moved past park, no own red verdict?}
    M -->|yes| CLR
    M -->|no| HOLD[Park holds — fail closed]
    CLR --> VA[validate-armed re-validates next pass]
```

</details>

Then headCommitActor on the new head returns the MERGE commit (committer sm-silent-update, date = merge time > park time). So `headTsVf > parkedTsVf` is TRUE. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. ## PR Description

Closes #750
### What changed
A MACHINE-authored PR parked on `validation_failed` now has a self-clear path: `update_branch`'s sticky-park RESET probe clears the label when the current head's check rollup is **green**, or the head **moved past the park** carrying no red dispatched verdict of its own — validate-armed re-validates normally on the next pass.

### Key decisions
- Implemented in the shared `update_branch` RESET probe, so both routes reach it: `silent-update-behind` (BEHIND heads) and `park-reset` (any merge state — the route fa#1227 actually rides)
- Machine-only: guests keep the 2026-09-27 sticky behavior (green-now and machine pushes clear nothing for them); a moved head with its **own** red verdict keeps the park (red never transfers across shas)
- Fail closed: probe failures (park time, actor, verdict) keep the park; the new branch is gated on the same non-null probes the human-push reset demands
- Verified ticket item (a): both `validation_failed` SET paths (`update_branch` sticky-park, `fail_validation` guest park) are guest-gated — the label on fa#1227 is legacy residue, no current rule labels machine PRs

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
```
7 new tests in the sticky-park suite: machine + green head self-clears (fa#1227 regression), head-moved-past-park self-clears, head predates park holds, own-red-verdict holds, probe failure holds (fail closed), guest sticky park untouched, park-reset rule route works.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    PR[Machine PR parked: validation_failed] --> PRST{park-reset rule}
    PRST --> R[update_branch RESET probe]
    R --> G{Head rollup GREEN?}
    G -->|yes| CLR[Remove label + clear comment]
    G -->|no| M{Head moved past park, no own red verdict?}
    M -->|yes| CLR
    M -->|no| HOLD[Park holds — fail closed]
    CLR --> VA[validate-armed re-validates next pass]
```

</details>

Now I understand the helpers. Key observations:

1. `validationRollupGreen(repoInfo, prNumber)` — uses `provider.prStatus(prNumber)` and checks `checkConclusion === 'green'`. Note: `prStatus` presumably is keyed to the current head. Fail closed (false on error). OK.

2. `headCommitActor` — returns `{login, date, committer, sha, parents}` or null. The `date` is `.committer.date`. Note the new code uses `headActorVf.date` — that's the committer date of the head commit. For a silent-update merge commit, committer date = when the SM ran silent update. So the headMovedCleanVf for a parked machine PR behind main: the SM silent-updates the branch (merge commit by sm-silent-update), which moves the head. Then headCommitActor on the new head returns the MERGE commit (committer sm-silent-update, date = merge time > park time). So `headTsVf > parkedTsVf` is TRUE. And latestDispatchedVerdict on the new sha — parked PRs get no CI dispatch, so null ≠ 'failure' → true. So headMovedCleanVf fires.

   So on the very first tick after the park was set (for a machine PR behind main), the sequence would be: park set (in the era when machine PRs could get labeled — legacy), then the next tick: update_branch runs (BEHIND), silent update moves the head, and the machine self-clear clears the label. That's per the ticket spec: "the park predates the last head move". OK, intended.

- **Updated**: 2026-10-05T18:48:53Z

## PR Description

Closes #750
### What changed
A MACHINE-authored PR parked on `validation_failed` now has a self-clear path: `update_branch`'s sticky-park RESET probe clears the label when the current head's check rollup is **green**, or the head **moved past the park** carrying no red dispatched verdict of its own — validate-armed re-validates normally on the next pass.

### Key decisions
- Implemented in the shared `update_branch` RESET probe, so both routes reach it: `silent-update-behind` (BEHIND heads) and `park-reset` (any merge state — the route fa#1227 actually rides)
- Machine-only: guests keep the 2026-09-27 sticky behavior (green-now and machine pushes clear nothing for them); a moved head with its **own** red verdict keeps the park (red never transfers across shas)
- Fail closed: probe failures (park time, actor, verdict) keep the park; the new branch is gated on the same non-null probes the human-push reset demands
- Verified ticket item (a): both `validation_failed` SET paths (`update_branch` sticky-park, `fail_validation` guest park) are guest-gated — the label on fa#1227 is legacy residue, no current rule labels machine PRs

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
```
7 new tests in the sticky-park suite: machine + green head self-clears (fa#1227 regression), head-moved-past-park self-clears, head predates park holds, own-red-verdict holds, probe failure holds (fail closed), guest sticky park untouched, park-reset rule route works.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    PR[Machine PR parked: validation_failed] --> PRST{park-reset rule}
    PRST --> R[update_branch RESET probe]
    R --> G{Head rollup GREEN?}
    G -->|yes| CLR[Remove label + clear comment]
    G -->|no| M{Head moved past park, no own red verdict?}
    M -->|yes| CLR
    M -->|no| HOLD[Park holds — fail closed]
    CLR --> VA[validate-armed re-validates next pass]
```

</details>

So the headMovedCleanVf for a parked machine PR behind main: the SM silent-updates the branch (merge commit by sm-silent-update), which moves the head. Then headCommitActor on the new head returns the MERGE commit (committer sm-silent-update, date = merge time > park time). So `headTsVf > parkedTsVf` is TRUE. And latestDispatchedVerdict on the new sha — parked PRs get no CI dispatch, so null ≠ 'failure' → true. So headMovedCleanVf fires.

   So on the very first tick after the park was set (for a machine PR behind main), the sequence would be: park set (in the era when machine PRs could get labeled — legacy), then the next tick: update_branch runs (BEHIND), silent update moves the head, and the machine self-clear clears the label. That's per the ticket spec: "the park predates the last head move". OK, intended.

## PR Description

Closes #750
### What changed
A MACHINE-authored PR parked on `validation_failed` now has a self-clear path: `update_branch`'s sticky-park RESET probe clears the label when the current head's check rollup is **green**, or the head **moved past the park** carrying no red dispatched verdict of its own — validate-armed re-validates normally on the next pass.

### Key decisions
- Implemented in the shared `update_branch` RESET probe, so both routes reach it: `silent-update-behind` (BEHIND heads) and `park-reset` (any merge state — the route fa#1227 actually rides)
- Machine-only: guests keep the 2026-09-27 sticky behavior (green-now and machine pushes clear nothing for them); a moved head with its **own** red verdict keeps the park (red never transfers across shas)
- Fail closed: probe failures (park time, actor, verdict) keep the park; the new branch is gated on the same non-null probes the human-push reset demands
- Verified ticket item (a): both `validation_failed` SET paths (`update_branch` sticky-park, `fail_validation` guest park) are guest-gated — the label on fa#1227 is legacy residue, no current rule labels machine PRs

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
```
7 new tests in the sticky-park suite: machine + green head self-clears (fa#1227 regression), head-moved-past-park self-clears, head predates park holds, own-red-verdict holds, probe failure holds (fail closed), guest sticky park untouched, park-reset rule route works.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD

    R --> G{Head rollup GREEN?}
    G -->|yes| CLR[Remove label + clear comment]

    M -->|yes| CLR
    M -->|no| HOLD[Park holds — fail closed]
    CLR --> VA[validate-armed re-validates next pass]
```

</details>

So the headMovedCleanVf for a parked machine PR behind main: the SM silent-updates the branch (merge commit by sm-silent-update), which moves the head. Then headCommitActor on the new head returns the MERGE commit (committer sm-silent-update, date = merge time > park time). So `headTsVf > parkedTsVf` is TRUE. re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for GitHub PR review…

- **Updated**: 2026-10-05T18:48:53Z

## PR Description

Closes #750
### What changed
A MACHINE-authored PR parked on `validation_failed` now has a self-clear path: `update_branch`'s sticky-park RESET probe clears the label when the current head's check rollup is **green**, or the head **moved past the park** carrying no red dispatched verdict of its own — validate-armed re-validates normally on the next pass.

### Key decisions
- Implemented in the shared `update_branch` RESET probe, so both routes reach it: `silent-update-behind` (BEHIND heads) and `park-reset` (any merge state — the route fa#1227 actually rides)
- Machine-only: guests keep the 2026-09-27 sticky behavior (green-now and machine pushes clear nothing for them); a moved head with its **own** red verdict keeps the park (red never transfers across shas)
- Fail closed: probe failures (park time, actor, verdict) keep the park; the new branch is gated on the same non-null probes the human-push reset demands
- Verified ticket item (a): both `validation_failed` SET paths (`update_branch` sticky-park, `fail_validation` guest park) are guest-gated — the label on fa#1227 is legacy residue, no current rule labels machine PRs

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
```
7 new tests in the sticky-park suite: machine + green head self-clears (fa#1227 regression), head-moved-past-park self-clears, head predates park holds, own-red-verdict holds, probe failure holds (fail closed), guest sticky park untouched, park-reset rule route works.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    PR[Machine PR parked: validation_failed] --> PRST{park-reset rule}
    PRST --> R[update_branch RESET probe]
    R --> G{Head rollup GREEN?}
    G -->|yes| CLR[Remove label + clear comment]
    G -->|no| M{Head moved past park, no own red verdict?}
    M -->|yes| CLR
    M -->|no| HOLD[Park holds — fail closed]
    CLR --> VA[validate-armed re-validates next pass]
```

</details>

## PR Description

Closes #750
### What changed
A MACHINE-authored PR parked on `validation_failed` now has a self-clear path: `update_branch`'s sticky-park RESET probe clears the label when the current head's check rollup is **green**, or the head **moved past the park** carrying no red dispatched verdict of its own — validate-armed re-validates normally on the next pass.

### Key decisions
- Implemented in the shared `update_branch` RESET probe, so both routes reach it: `silent-update-behind` (BEHIND heads) and `park-reset` (any merge state — the route fa#1227 actually rides)
- Machine-only: guests keep the 2026-09-27 sticky behavior (green-now and machine pushes clear nothing for them); a moved head with its **own** red verdict keeps the park (red never transfers across shas)
- Fail closed: probe failures (park time, actor, verdict) keep the park; the new branch is gated on the same non-null probes the human-push reset demands
- Verified ticket item (a): both `validation_failed` SET paths (`update_branch` sticky-park, `fail_validation` guest park) are guest-gated — the label on fa#1227 is legacy residue, no current rule labels machine PRs

```bash

## PR Description

Closes #750
### What changed
A MACHINE-authored PR parked on `validation_failed` now has a self-clear path: `update_branch`'s sticky-park RESET probe clears the label when the current head's check rollup is **green**, or the head **moved past the park** carrying no red dispatched verdict of its own — validate-armed re-validates normally on the next pass.

### Key decisions
- Implemented in the shared `update_branch` RESET probe, so both routes reach it: `silent-update-behind` (BEHIND heads) and `park-reset` (any merge state — the route fa#1227 actually rides)
- Machine-only: guests keep the 2026-09-27 sticky behavior (green-now and machine pushes clear nothing for them); a moved head with its **own** red verdict keeps the park (red never transfers across shas)
- Fail closed: probe failures (park time, actor, verdict) keep the park; the new branch is gated on the same non-null probes the human-push reset demands
- Verified ticket item (a): both `validation_failed` SET paths (`update_branch` sticky-park, `fail_validation` guest park) are guest-gated — the label on fa#1227 is legacy residue, no current rule labels machine PRs

### How to verify
```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
```
7 new tests in the sticky-park suite: machine + green head self-clears (fa#1227 regression), head-moved-past-park self-clears, head predates park holds, own-red-verdict holds, probe failure holds (fail closed), guest sticky park untouched, park-reset rule route works.

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    PR[Machine PR parked: validation_failed] --> PRST{park-reset rule}
    PRST --> R[update_branch RESET probe]
    R --> G{Head rollup GREEN?}
    G -->|yes| CLR[Remove label + clear comment]
    G -->|no| M{Head moved past park, no own red verdict?}
    M -->|yes| CLR
    M -->|no| HOLD[Park holds — fail closed]
    CLR --> VA[validate-armed re-validates next pass]
```

</details>

Now I understand the helpers. Key observations:

1. `validationRollupGreen(repoInfo, prNumber)` — uses `provider.prStatus(prNumber)` and checks `checkConclusion === 'green'`. Note: `prStatus` presumably is keyed to the current head. Fail closed (false on error). OK.

2. `headCommitActor` — returns `{login, date, committer, sha, parents}` or null. The `date` is `.committer.date`. Note the new code uses `headActorVf.date` — that's the committer date of the head commit. For a silent-update merge commit, committer date = when the SM ran silent update. So the headMovedCleanVf for a parked machine PR behind main: the SM silent-updates the branch (merge commit by sm-silent-update), which moves the head. Then headCommitActor on the new head returns the MERGE commit (committer sm-silent-update, date = merge time > park time). So `headTsVf > parkedTsVf` is TRUE. And latestDispatchedVerdict on the new sha — parked PRs get no CI dispatch, so null ≠ 'failure' → true. So headMovedCleanVf fires.

   So on the very first tick after the park was set (for a machine PR behind main), the sequence would be: park set (in the era when machine PRs could get labeled — legacy), then the next tick: update_branch runs (BEHIND), silent update moves the head, and the machine self-clear clears the label.
